sentences.text: Paraortygoides is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the family Gallinuloididae.
The type species of the genus Paraortygoides is Paraortygoides messelensis — the species the genus is based on.
A second species, Paraortygoides argillae, was described by Mayr and Kitchener in 2024.
Fossils of the type species Paraortygoides messelensis have been found in the Messel Formation of Germany.
The species Paraortygoides argillae occurred in the Walton Member of the London Clay Formation in England.
The Paleobi Database classifies Paraortygoides under the class Reptilia.
This bird lived in Europe during the Ypresian and Lutetian stages of the Eocene epoch.
The time range for Paraortygoides is recorded as the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
